content.aim: To investigate plate clutch friction experiment.
objectives: (1) To investigate the relationship between friction torque T and the axial load W applied to a single plate clutch. (2) To obtain the coefficient of friction between the two rubbing surfaces, assuming uniform wear. (3) To verify that the friction torque is proportional to the mean radius of the friction disc.
apparatus: The plate clutch friction apparatus has a mild steel top plate that is loaded axially with weights, a lower plate with locating pegs that holds the friction disc, three Ferodo friction discs of different sizes, and cords with hangers over pulleys on the top plate to apply the pure couple. Check that all traces of oil are removed from the machined surfaces before fitting the Ferodo disc (plain side up), and never allow the machined surface of the top plate to come into direct contact with the locating pegs fitted in the lower plate.

theory.text:
The single plate clutch

A plate clutch transmits torque between two rotating shafts through the friction between a friction disc (a ring of lining material, such as Ferodo) and a steel plate, which are pressed together by an axial force W. The friction disc is an annulus of inner radius R₁ and outer radius R₂ (). The torque that it can transmit before slipping is the friction torque.

: Plate clutch apparatus and the friction disc (schematic)

Friction torque for uniform wear

Take a ring of radius r and width dr on the disc. If p is the pressure on it, the normal force is dN = p · 2πr dr, and the friction torque contributed by the ring is dT = μ dN · r = μ p 2πr² dr. For a clutch that has worn in, the wear is uniform, which means that p r = C is constant, so the load is W = ∫ p 2πr dr = 2πC (R₂ − R₁). Therefore C = W/[2π(R₂ − R₁)] and

T = ∫ μ C 2πr dr = π μ C (R₂² − R₁²) = μ W (R₁ + R₂) / 2 = μ W R

where R = (R₁ + R₂)/2 is the mean radius of the disc. This has three consequences: (a) for a given disc, T is proportional to W, so a graph of T against W is a straight line through the origin; (b) the gradient is T/W = μ R, which gives μ; (c) for a fixed W and coefficient of friction, T/R = μ W is constant, so the torque is proportional to the mean radius R of the disc. In this experiment, the axial load W includes the weight of the top plate.

Uniform pressure

For a new clutch, the pressure is more nearly uniform, and the torque is T = (2/3) μ W (R₂³ − R₁³)/(R₂² − R₁²). This is slightly larger than μ W R when R₁ is much smaller than R₂, and for a narrow ring the two are almost the same, so the uniform wear assumption is usually the safer basis for design (it gives the lower torque capacity).

Measuring the torque

A pure couple is applied to the top plate by two equal weights m on cords over pulleys, with the effective diameter D of the top plate as the arm. When the plate turns at a very slow, steady speed, the applied torque just balances the friction torque:

T = m g D

precautions: The friction torque increased in proportion to the axial load on each disc.
For the same load, the larger disc needed a larger torque.
Slow, steady rotation of the top plate is hard to hold, and the plate sometimes sticks and slips (stick–slip).
Remove all traces of oil from the machined surfaces before fitting the disc, since oil lowers the friction; keep the disc concentric with the top plate.
Make sure that the top plate rotates at the same very slow constant speed for each reading (time one revolution of a cord pulley), and do not let the machined plate touch the locating pegs.
content.discussion: Sources of error: the speed of the top plate is not exactly constant, and the torque needed to just keep it moving is judged by eye, with the weights in steps; the friction in the pulleys and the cords adds to the apparent torque; the mean radius is found from measured radii (±0.2 mm); the disc surface may not be fully run in, so the pressure distribution differs from uniform wear; temperature rises from rubbing reduce μ; oil or dust on the surfaces affects μ; and the weight of the top plate must be added to W. [Compare your μ with 0.25, and say whether T ∝ W and T ∝ R are verified within the error.]
content.conclusion: Results validated the theoretical relationships described above.
learnings: Applied theoretical principles to experimental measurement.
